thread:
Alex: Ran an nsys profile on latest main after the batching heuristic tweak (commit abc1234). Seeing large read amplification in the KV path — kernel `kv_load_v2` is now dominating the timeline. cc @Maria @Ryan
Maria: Can you paste the timeline / flame / top kernels? Any before/after traces to compare?
Alex: Pasted the quick TL;DR and commands. Command I used: `nsys profile -o /tmp/after -t cuda,osrt ./runner --workload=hf-small --trace`
```
# top kernels (after - commit abc1234)
kv_load_v2               42.3 ms  (was 6.1 ms before)
memcpy_h2d               8.7 ms
batch_dispatch           3.2 ms
other_kernels            1.1 ms
```
Artifacts: s3://redwood-traces/1719456789/after.nsys  (after), s3://redwood-traces/1719456789/before.nsys  (baseline)
Ryan: Huh. +36ms in `kv_load_v2` is pretty large. Could be we regressed prefix cache hit behavior or changed the lookup ordering so we traverse more entries per request. Did you run `trace_diff.py`?
Alex: Yup — ran `scripts/trace_diff.py before.nsys after.nsys` — diff shows a lot more time spent in `kv_lookup_loop` for cold prefixes and higher memcpy counts. Also collected an nvprof callstack:
```
# nvprof sample (after)
  kv_load_v2 -> kv_lookup -> memcpy (hot) -> device_atomic
# nvprof sample (before)
  kv_load_v2 -> fast_path_lookup -> memcpy (small)
```
Maria: Can you bisect the commits between which the batching heuristic change landed? Put the range here and we'll kick off a bisect job.
Alex: Range: abc1234..def5678. I started a quick local binary search and saw the jump after commit def2345 (`optimize-batcher-reorder`).
Jamal: I can run a CI bisect job. How many commits in that range?
Alex: ~18. Steps I used locally: `git bisect start def5678 abc1234` -> checkout candidate -> run small nsys profile script `ci/perf/nsys_smoke.sh` -> check `kv_load_v2` median.
ci-bot: Started bisect job #4821 (runner=bisect-2). Logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/4821
Maria: Also upload perfetto slices — there's a spike at ~2.0s where memcpy bursts align with the kv timeline. Perfetto link: perfetto://redwood/trace/1719456789/after (screenshot attached)
Sasha: This smells like the batching heuristic increased average batch depth which amplifies per-request traversal. Try forcing `batch_max=8` and `kv_prefetch=true` to see if it mitigates. Config snippet I used: ```json
{ "batch_max": 8, "kv_prefetch": true }
```
Alex: Good call — forcing `batch_max=8` drops `kv_load_v2` back down to ~8ms in my local run. That strongly implicates the reorder in `optimize-batcher-reorder`. I'll continue the bisect and open a PR to revert.
Alex (update 20m later): Bisect found culprit: commit def2345 (optimize-batcher-reorder). Reverting that commit in a local build restores before numbers. Opened PR with revert + regression test: https://github.com/redwood/ri/pull/4567
Maria: Great — please add a perf unit test that runs small nsys smoke and asserts `kv_load_v2` median < 15ms for the hf-small workload. Put artifacts into the ci bucket.
Alex: Will add test + perf thresholds. Final numbers I recorded: before = 6.1ms, after-regression = 42.3ms, revert = 7.2ms. Uploaded final traces: s3://redwood-traces/1719456789/{before,after,revert}.nsys. Closing local investigation, leaving CI bisect artifacts in job #4821. :thumbsup:
Ryan: Nice work, thanks for the quick turnaround. When PR merges we should run a full perf run across a couple longer workloads to be safe.
